pitch.text: Retrieval-augmented readers treat every retrieved passage as equally trustworthy; this paper shows a tiny gate in front of the reader buys 2-3 EM points,
which makes it a good case for asking whether cheap filtering beats bigger readers.

why.text: The pipeline figure: point at where the gate sits between retriever and reader, then ask what it can never fix — a passage the retriever missed.

spans.text: That the relevant passage is among those retrieved: the gate can only down-weight, never recover, evidence,
and the paper never measures how often retrieval misses.

questions.text: Is the gate doing anything a reranker on the retriever's scores could not?
Why does the gain double on multi-hop HotpotQA?
Would you trust gains measured only on development sets?
What happens when the gate is trained on one benchmark and used on another?
Is a 0.3 EM lead within ±0.4 a result?

for.text: Consistent gains on two benchmarks against re-run baselines.
The adapter is 40% smaller than the one it beats.

against.text: No test-set numbers; the development sets also chose the model.
The gate is retrained per benchmark, so the method is less general than it looks.
